case_number: CA No. 901 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (C) No. 9927 of 2020)
summary: The key issue was whether an Award passed by a Lok Adalat under Section 20 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, based on a compromise, can serve as the basis for invoking Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for redetermination of compensation. The High Court held that the Lok Adalat Award, being deemed a decree under Section 21 of the 1987 Act, enables similarly situated landowners to claim enhanced compensation. The appellant contended that Section 28A requires a judicial determination by a court under the 1894 Act, and that Lok Adalat Awards, being based on compromise, lack adjudicatory character. The respondents argued that the deeming fiction under Section 21 must be given full effect to ensure substantive justice and equality. The Supreme Court considered the scope of legal fictions, legislative intent behind Section 28A, and the binding nature of Lok Adalat Awards.
legal_provisions_cited: State of Punjab v. Jalour Singh
Government of India v. Vedanta Limited
Attar Singh v. Union of India
Tahera Khatoon (D) by LRs. v. State of Bihar
final_judgment: The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's judgment, holding that the Award of the Lok Adalat, being deemed a decree of a civil court under Section 21 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, can form the basis for invoking Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, thereby entitling similarly situated landowners to enhanced compensation.
